tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 1
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A cube-shaped resin block has mass $M(s)=5s^{3}$ grams when its side length is $s>0$ cm. Increasing the side from $2$ cm to $3$ cm adds exactly $95$ grams of mass.
A factory models daily output by $Q(L)=20L^{1/2}$ units for $L>0$ labour-hours. Raising labour from $16$ to $64$ hours makes output more than three times as large.
A clinic uses $T(m)=18m^{-1/4}$ hours to model clearance time for a patient of mass $m>0$ kg. Moving from $m=16$ to $m=81$ reduces the predicted time by exactly one third.
A road engineer models stopping distance by $d(v)=0.08v^{2}$ metres at speed $v>0$ m/s. Raising speed from $15$ to $18$ m/s increases stopping distance by exactly $40\%$.
A manufacturer estimates a spherical tank's coating cost by $C(r)=12r^{2}$ dollars for radius $r>0$. Doubling the tank's diameter multiplies the coating cost by exactly $4$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
M(2)&=5(2)^3=40,\quad M(3)=5(3)^3=135 \\ M(3)-M(2)&=135-40=95
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q(16)&=20(4)=80,\quad Q(64)=20(8)=160 \\ \frac{Q(64)}{Q(16)}&=2<3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
T(16)&=18(16)^{-1/4}=9,\quad T(81)=18(81)^{-1/4}=6 \\ \frac{9-6}{9}&=\frac13
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d(18)}{d(15)}&=\left(\frac{18}{15}\right)^2=1.44 \\ (1.44-1)100\%&=44\%\ne40\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{C(2r)}{C(r)}&=\frac{12(2r)^2}{12r^2}=2^2=4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Applied evaluation and exact changes in power-law models.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 2
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A workshop follows $Q(L)=9L^{2/3}$ for $L>0$ labour-hours. Increasing labour from $8$ to $27$ hours raises output by exactly $150\%$.
A lamp produces illuminance $I(d)=720d^{-2}$ lux at distance $d>0$ metres. Moving a sensor from $6$ metres to $12$ metres lowers its reading by exactly $75\%$.
A technician's learning curve is $H(n)=48n^{-1/3}$ hours for unit number $n>0$. Moving from the $8$th to the $64$th unit reduces completion time by exactly $75\%$.
A biologist models an animal's load-bearing strength as proportional to $L^{2}$ and mass as proportional to $L^{3}$. Scaling every length by $1.5$ multiplies strength per unit mass by exactly $2/3$.
A computing team models processing time by $T(N)=3N^{3/2}$ seconds for $N>0$ records. Expanding a job from $100$ to $400$ records multiplies processing time by exactly $6$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q(8)&=9(4)=36,\quad Q(27)=9(9)=81 \\ \frac{81-36}{36}100\%&=125\%\ne150\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(6)&=20,\quad I(12)=5 \\ \frac{20-5}{20}100\%&=75\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(8)&=48(8)^{-1/3}=24,\quad H(64)=12 \\ \frac{24-12}{24}100\%&=50\%\ne75\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\text{strength}}{\text{mass}}&\propto\frac{L^2}{L^3}=L^{-1} \\ (1.5)^{-1}&=\frac23
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{T(400)}{T(100)}&=\left(\frac{400}{100}\right)^{3/2}=4^{3/2}=8\ne6
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Scale factors for production, illumination, learning, strength, and computation.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 3
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A tank holds $V(h)=2h^{3/2}$ litres when the fluid depth is $h\ge0$ metres. A measured volume of $54$ litres corresponds to a depth of exactly $9$ metres.
A sensor calibration uses $C(x)=96x^{-2}$ for a positive setting $x$. When the display reads $C=6$, the technician claims that the setting must be $x=2$.
A pendulum model gives period $P(L)=0.5L^{1/2}$ seconds for length $L\ge0$ cm. A period of $3$ seconds requires a length of exactly $36$ cm.
A pressure gauge is calibrated by the real equation $y^{4}=81$. The laboratory report states that the equation has exactly one real calibration, namely $y=3$.
A growth model has the form $G(t)=At^{r}$ for $t>0$, with $A>0$. Measurements $G(1)=6$ and $G(4)=48$ determine $A=6$ and $r=3/2$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
2h^{3/2}&=54\Rightarrow h^{3/2}=27 \\ h&=27^{2/3}=9
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
96x^{-2}&=6\Rightarrow x^{-2}=\frac1{16} \\ x^2&=16,\quad x=4\ne2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
0.5\sqrt L&=3\Rightarrow\sqrt L=6 \\ L&=36
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
y^4&=81=3^4 \\ y&=3\ \text{or}\ y=-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=G(1)=6 \\ 6(4)^r&=48\Rightarrow4^r=8=4^{3/2}\Rightarrow r=\frac32
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Solving applied power equations and recovering model parameters.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 4
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A courier assigns package weight $w(n)=3n$ kg for $n$ crates and cost $C(w)=2w^{2}$ dollars. For $4$ crates, the composed model $C(w(4))$ gives exactly $96$ dollars.
A circular stain has radius $r(t)=\sqrt{t+1}$ cm after $t\ge0$ minutes and area $A(r)=\pi r^{2}$. After $8$ minutes, the composed area model gives exactly $9\pi$ square centimetres.
A staffing model first predicts cases $c(d)=5d^{3}$ on day $d>0$, then workload $W(c)=2\sqrt c$. On day $4$, the composed workload is exactly $40$ units.
A machine's chamber volume is $v(t)=2t$ litres at setting $t>0$, while pressure is $p(v)=4v^{-1}$ bar. At setting $t=3$, the composed pressure is exactly $2/3$ bar.
A route model gives signed displacement $d(t)=t^{2}$ and a reporting rule $R(d)=\sqrt d$. At time $t=-3$, the composition $R(d(t))$ returns the signed value $-3$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
w(4)&=3(4)=12 \\ C(w(4))&=2(12)^2=288\ne96
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
r(8)&=\sqrt9=3 \\ A(r(8))&=\pi(3)^2=9\pi
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
c(4)&=5(4)^3=320 \\ W(c(4))&=2\sqrt{320}=16\sqrt5\ne40
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
v(3)&=6 \\ p(v(3))&=4(6)^{-1}=\frac23
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(d(-3))&=\sqrt{(-3)^2}=\sqrt9=3 \\ 3&\ne-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Composition of power-based models with domain and sign traps.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 5
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: An architect models the height of a semicircular arch by $h(x)=\sqrt{25-x^{2}}$ metres. The real horizontal positions accepted by the model are exactly $-5\le x\le5$.
A signed dose adjustment is recorded as $D(t)=t^{2/3}$ using real cube roots. A consultant claims that the formula has no real value when the adjustment $t$ is negative.
A concentration model is $C(v)=10v^{-1/2}$ for a sample volume $v$. Its exact real domain is $v>0$, so a zero-volume input must be rejected.
A signal processor uses $S(t)=(-t)^{1/2}$ with real outputs. Its manual claims that every nonnegative time $t\ge0$ is an allowed input.
An economist defines utility by $U(q)=q^{5/4}$ using the conventional real fourth root. The quantity input must satisfy $q\ge0$ for the utility to be real.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
25-x^2&\ge0\Rightarrow x^2\le25 \\ -5&\le x\le5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
D(t)&=(\sqrt[3]{t})^2 \\ D(-8)&=(-2)^2=4\in\mathbb R
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
C(v)&=\frac{10}{\sqrt v} \\ \sqrt v&\ \text{must be real and nonzero}\Rightarrow v>0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
q^{5/4}&=(\sqrt[4]{q})^5 \\ \sqrt[4]{q}\in\mathbb R&\Rightarrow q\ge0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Real domains of fractional and negative power models.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 6
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Two algorithms require $A(n)=4n^{1.4}$ and $B(n)=100n^{1.2}$ operations for $n>0$. An engineer claims that $B$ still requires more operations when $n=10^{10}$.
Two liquid doses have normalized strengths $x^{1/2}$ and $x^{3}$ for $0<x<1$. Throughout this interval, the square-root dose is strictly stronger than the cubic dose.
Competing contamination models are $A(t)=3t^{-2}$ and $B(t)=2t^{-1}$ for $t>0$. A report claims that $A(t)$ remains larger than $B(t)$ for all sufficiently large $t$.
A file-processing model is $T(n)=n^{5/4}$ seconds for $n>0$. Doubling the file size multiplies processing time by more than $2$ but less than $2.5$.
A filter's concentration response is $R(c)=c^{-1/3}$ for $c>0$. Raising concentration from $8$ to $64$ makes the response exactly one quarter as large.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{A(10^{10})}{B(10^{10})}&=\frac4{100}(10^{10})^{0.2} \\ &=0.04(100)=4>1
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
0<x<1,\quad \frac12&<3 \\ x^{1/2}&>x^3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{A(t)}{B(t)}&=\frac{3t^{-2}}{2t^{-1}}=\frac{3}{2t} \\ \frac{3}{2t}&\to0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{T(2n)}{T(n)}&=2^{5/4}=2\sqrt[4]2 \\ 2&<2^{5/4}\approx2.378<2.5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{R(64)}{R(8)}&=\left(\frac{64}{8}\right)^{-1/3}=8^{-1/3}=\frac12\ne\frac14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Comparing power-law growth and decay across scales.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 7
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A circular panel has area model $A(r)=7r^{2}$ for radius $r>0$. Increasing the radius by $12\%$ increases the modeled area by exactly $25.44\%$.
A retailer models demand by $q(p)=500p^{-3/2}$ for price $p>0$. Raising price by $10\%$ reduces demand by exactly $15\%$, not merely approximately.
A farm uses $Q(L)=40L^{0.6}$ with all other inputs fixed. For a small $5\%$ labour increase, the first-order elasticity estimate predicts an output increase of about $3\%$.
A spherical balloon has volume proportional to $r^{3}$. Reducing its radius by $20\%$ reduces its volume by exactly $60\%$.
A detector follows the inverse-square model $I(d)=kd^{-2}$ for $d>0$. Increasing distance by $25\%$ reduces the detected intensity by exactly $36\%$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{A(1.12r)}{A(r)}&=(1.12)^2=1.2544 \\ (1.2544-1)100\%&=25.44\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{q(1.1p)}{q(p)}&=1.1^{-3/2}\approx0.86678 \\ \text{decrease}&\approx13.32\%\ne15\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dQ}{Q}&\approx0.6\frac{dL}{L} \\ 0.6(5\%)&=3\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{V(0.8r)}{V(r)}&=(0.8)^3=0.512 \\ \text{decrease}&=(1-0.512)100\%=48.8\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{I(1.25d)}{I(d)}&=(1.25)^{-2}=0.64 \\ \text{decrease}&=(1-0.64)100\%=36\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Exact and approximate percentage changes in power laws.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 8
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A position sensor uses $y=3x^{2}$ for every real $x$. Its software claims that $x=\sqrt{y/3}$ recovers every real position that could have produced a positive reading.
A calibration curve is $y=4x^{5}$ for real $x$. Because the fifth power is one-to-one, its inverse is $x=(y/4)^{1/5}$ for every real reading $y$.
A positive production run $q$ has unit cost $C=12/q$. A manager rearranges the model and claims that the inverse rule is $q=12C$.
A vessel's volume-depth relation is $V=\tfrac12h^{3/2}$ for $h\ge0$. Solving for depth gives the inverse formula $h=(2V)^{2/3}$ for $V\ge0$.
A braking model is $d=5v^{2}$ with signed velocity $v\in\mathbb R$. An analyst says $v=\sqrt{d/5}$ is an inverse that recovers every possible signed velocity.
tactical_explanations:
**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
C&=\frac{12}{q}\Rightarrow Cq=12 \\ q&=\frac{12}{C}\ne12C
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Inverse functions and the role of restricted domains.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 9
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A firm uses $Q(L,K)=12L^{0.4}K^{0.6}$ for positive labour and capital. Increasing both inputs by $50\%$ increases output by exactly $50\%$.
A plant uses $Q(L,K)=10L^{0.7}K^{0.5}$. A supervisor claims that doubling both positive inputs makes output less than twice as large.
A farm follows $Q(L,K)=30L^{1/2}K^{1/4}$. Multiplying labour by $4$ and capital by $16$ multiplies output by exactly $4$.
A workshop has output $Q(L)=8L^{3/4}$ for $L>0$. To reach output $Q=64$, a planner claims that exactly $L=8$ units of labour are required.
A firm's total cost is $C(q)=200q^{0.8}$ for output $q>0$. Its average cost $C(q)/q$ falls by the factor $2^{-0.2}$ whenever output doubles.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(1.5L,1.5K)}{Q(L,K)}&=(1.5)^{0.4+0.6}=1.5 \\ \text{increase}&=50\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(2L,2K)}{Q(L,K)}&=2^{0.7+0.5}=2^{1.2} \\ 2^{1.2}&>2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(4L,16K)}{Q(L,K)}&=4^{1/2}16^{1/4} \\ &=2\cdot2=4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
8L^{3/4}&=64\Rightarrow L^{3/4}=8 \\ L&=8^{4/3}=16\ne8
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Returns to scale and input changes in production models.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 10
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A designer enlarges every linear dimension of a model cylinder by a factor of $3$. She claims that both its surface area and its volume become exactly $9$ times as large.
A family of similar aquariums has water mass proportional to the cube of linear size. Enlarging every length by $2.5$ multiplies the water mass by exactly $15.625$.
A cable obeys $R=\rho L/A$. A redesign multiplies both its length and diameter by $4$, and an engineer claims that its electrical resistance is unchanged.
An animal model gives body mass proportional to $L^{3}$ and limb strength proportional to $L^{2}$. Doubling size halves the strength-to-mass ratio.
For a sphere, surface-to-volume ratio equals $3/r$. A lab report claims that tripling the radius reduces this ratio to one ninth of its original value.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{S_{\text{new}}}{S_{\text{old}}}&=3^2=9 \\ \frac{V_{\text{new}}}{V_{\text{old}}}&=3^3=27\ne9
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{m_{\text{new}}}{m_{\text{old}}}&=(2.5)^3=15.625
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{L_{\text{new}}}{L}&=4,\quad\frac{A_{\text{new}}}{A}=4^2=16 \\ \frac{R_{\text{new}}}{R}&=\frac4{16}=\frac14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\text{strength}}{\text{mass}}&\propto L^{-1} \\ \frac{(2L)^{-1}}{L^{-1}}&=\frac12
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{(S/V)_{\text{new}}}{(S/V)_{\text{old}}}&=\frac{3/(3r)}{3/r}=\frac13\ne\frac19
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Geometric similarity and physical power-law scaling.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 11
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A kinetic model assigns energy $E(m)=2m^{5/2}$ joules to a positive mass index $m$. At $m=9$, the model returns exactly $486$ joules.
A concentration setting $x>0$ satisfies $7x^{-3}=56$. A technician solves the equation and records the setting as $x=2$.
A model uses $R(t)=(-t)^{4/3}$ with real cube roots. At the signed input $t=-8$, the reported value is exactly $16$.
A lab fits $P(x)=Ax^{r}$ from readings $P(2)=12$ and $P(8)=96$, with $A>0$. The report concludes that $r=3/2$ and $A=3$.
A two-stage rule first computes $g(x)=8x^{6}$ and then $f(u)=u^{1/3}$ using real cube roots. The composition satisfies $f(g(x))=2x^{2}$ for every real $x$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
E(9)&=2(9)^{5/2}=2(\sqrt9)^5 \\ &=2(3^5)=486
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
7x^{-3}&=56\Rightarrow x^{-3}=8 \\ x^3&=\frac18\Rightarrow x=\frac12\ne2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(-8)&=(8)^{4/3}=(\sqrt[3]8)^4 \\ &=2^4=16
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{96}{12}&=\left(\frac82\right)^r\Rightarrow8=4^r\Rightarrow r=\frac32 \\ A&=\frac{12}{2^{3/2}}=3\sqrt2\ne3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(g(x))&=(8x^6)^{1/3}=2(x^6)^{1/3} \\ &=2x^2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Mixed evaluation, equation solving, parameter fitting, and composition.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 12
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A light meter follows $I(d)=1600d^{-2}$ lux. Moving it from $20$ metres to $40$ metres lowers the reading by exactly $2$ lux.
An orbital model gives period $T(a)=3a^{3/2}$ days for radius index $a>0$. Raising $a$ from $4$ to $16$ multiplies the period by exactly $8$.
At fixed temperature, a gas model is $P(V)=600V^{-1}$ kPa. Increasing volume from $20$ to $25$ litres decreases pressure by exactly $25\%$.
A vehicle's kinetic energy is proportional to $v^{2}$. Raising speed by $30\%$ increases kinetic energy by exactly $69\%$ when mass is fixed.
A dosing rule is $c(w)=40w^{-1/2}$ for weight $w>0$. Multiplying patient weight by $4$ reduces the recommended concentration to one quarter.

**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(20)&=4,\quad I(40)=1 \\ I(20)-I(40)&=3\ne2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{T(16)}{T(4)}&=\left(\frac{16}{4}\right)^{3/2}=4^{3/2}=8
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(20)&=30,\quad P(25)=24 \\ \frac{30-24}{30}100\%&=20\%\ne25\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{K(1.3v)}{K(v)}&=(1.3)^2=1.69 \\ \text{increase}&=69\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{c(4w)}{c(w)}&=4^{-1/2}=\frac12\ne\frac14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Inverse and direct power laws in applied science.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 13
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A tidal-force model is $F(d)=18d^{-3}$ for distance $d>0$. Moving from distance $2$ to distance $6$ reduces the modeled force to exactly $1/27$ of its previous value.
An email campaign follows $N(t)=100\cdot2^{t}$ subscribers after $t$ weeks. A report classifies this as a power function $At^{r}$ of time because its output doubles regularly.
A parking garage charges $C(x)=5x^{0}$ dollars for every positive parking duration $x$. The graph on $x>0$ is the horizontal line $C=5$.
A machine calibration requires $(3x)^{4}=1296$ for a real control $x$. The technician claims that the equation has only the solution $x=2$.
A risk score is $R(x)=x^{-4/3}$ using real cube roots. Its real domain includes every negative $x$ but excludes $x=0$.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
N(t)&=100\cdot2^t \\ \frac{N(2t)}{N(t)}&=2^t\ \text{is not a constant }2^r
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
x^0&=1\quad(x>0) \\ C(x)&=5(1)=5
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
(3x)^4&=1296=6^4 \\ 3x&=\pm6\Rightarrow x=\pm2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(x)&=\frac1{(\sqrt[3]x)^4} \\ \sqrt[3]x&\ \text{exists for all real }x,\quad x\ne0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Recognizing power functions and handling fractional-power equations.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 14
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A manufacturer models batch cost by $C(q)=80q^{3/4}$ for $q>0$. Increasing batch size from $16$ to $81$ makes total cost exactly three times as large.
A pollutant index is $D(c)=12c^{-2}$ for concentration control $c>0$. Reducing the control by $25\%$ multiplies the index by exactly $16/9$.
A growth curve is $f(x)=x^{7/2}$ for $x>0$. An analyst claims that its slope decreases as $x$ increases because the exponent is fractional.
A material test produces the real equation $x^{2/5}=9$. The test has exactly two real inputs, $x=-243$ and $x=243$.
A seller faces demand $q(p)=100p^{-2}$, so revenue is $R(p)=pq(p)$. Raising price by $25\%$ lowers revenue by exactly $25\%$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{C(81)}{C(16)}&=\left(\frac{81}{16}\right)^{3/4} \\ &=\left(\frac32\right)^3=\frac{27}{8}\ne3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
f'(x)&=\frac72x^{5/2} \\ f''(x)&=\frac{35}{4}x^{3/2}>0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sqrt[5]x)^2&=9\Rightarrow\sqrt[5]x=\pm3 \\ x&=(\pm3)^5=\pm243
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(p)&=100p^{-1} \\ \frac{R(1.25p)}{R(p)}&=(1.25)^{-1}=0.8
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Cost, elasticity, monotonicity, equations, and revenue.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 15
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A firm uses $Q(L,K)=100L^{0.3}K^{0.7}$ with positive inputs. Raising both labour and capital by $20\%$ raises output by exactly $20\%$.
A workshop uses $Q(L,K)=L^{0.4}K^{0.4}$. Because both exponents are positive, a manager claims that doubling both inputs exactly doubles output.
A production process is $Q(L,K)=6L^{1/3}K^{2/3}$. With capital fixed, multiplying labour by $8$ multiplies output by exactly $2$.
A single-input plant follows $Q(L)=5L^{2/3}$ for $L>0$. A planner claims that output $Q=45$ requires exactly $L=81$ units of labour.
A balanced process has $Q(L,K)=20L^{1/2}K^{1/2}$. Multiplying labour by $4$ while dividing capital by $4$ leaves output unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(1.2L,1.2K)}{Q(L,K)}&=1.2^{0.3+0.7}=1.2 \\ \text{increase}&=20\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(2L,2K)}{Q(L,K)}&=2^{0.4+0.4}=2^{0.8} \\ 2^{0.8}&\ne2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(8L,K)}{Q(L,K)}&=8^{1/3}=2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
5L^{2/3}&=45\Rightarrow L^{2/3}=9 \\ L&=9^{3/2}=27\ne81
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Q(4L,K/4)}{Q(L,K)}&=4^{1/2}\left(\frac14\right)^{1/2} \\ &=2\cdot\frac12=1
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Cobb-Douglas returns, thresholds, and offsetting input changes.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 16
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A coding rule maps $x$ to $y=x^{3}/27$ for real $x$. A programmer claims that its inverse is $x=9y^{1/3}$.
A wire obeys $R=\rho L/A$. A similar redesign triples both length and diameter, so the new resistance is exactly one third of the old resistance.
For similar thermal stores, heat loss capacity scales with surface area $L^{2}$ while stored heat scales with volume $L^{3}$. Enlarging size by $4$ cuts their ratio to one sixteenth.
A cleanup model gives pollutant level $c(t)=5t^{-2/3}$ for $t>0$. Multiplying cleanup time by $8$ reduces the level to exactly one quarter.
A symmetric material response is $f(x)=|x|^{5}$. A report claims that this response equals the ordinary power $x^{5}$ for every real input.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{L_{\text{new}}}{L}&=3,\quad\frac{A_{\text{new}}}{A}=3^2=9 \\ \frac{R_{\text{new}}}{R}&=\frac39=\frac13
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{c(8t)}{c(t)}&=8^{-2/3}=(\sqrt[3]8)^{-2} \\ &=2^{-2}=\frac14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
x<0&\Rightarrow |x|^5>0 \\ x<0&\Rightarrow x^5<0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Inverse cubes, resistance, similarity, decay, and absolute values.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 17
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Two sensors use $f(x)=2x^{2}$ and $g(x)=9x^{2}$ for $x>0$. Doubling the input produces the same factor of increase in both sensor readings.
A field study fits $P(t)=At^{r}$ from $P(2)=40$ and $P(8)=320$. The researcher concludes that the power exponent is $r=3$.
A free-fall model is $s(t)=4.9t^{2}$ metres. The distance fallen by $5$ seconds is exactly $6.25$ times the distance fallen by $2$ seconds.
A real calibration equation is $x^{4/3}=16$, interpreted through real cube roots. A technician claims that its complete solution set is only $\{8\}$.
Two positive doses satisfy $0<a<b$, and response is modeled by $R(x)=x^{-2}$. The smaller dose $a$ produces the larger modeled response.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{f(2x)}{f(x)}&=2^2=4 \\ \frac{g(2x)}{g(x)}&=2^2=4
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{320}{40}&=\left(\frac82\right)^r \\ 8&=4^r\Rightarrow r=\frac32\ne3
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{s(5)}{s(2)}&=\left(\frac52\right)^2=\frac{25}{4}=6.25
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sqrt[3]x)^4&=16\Rightarrow\sqrt[3]x=\pm2 \\ x&=\pm8
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Scale ratios, fitted exponents, free fall, and negative exponents.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 18
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A learning model is $H(n)=60n^{-1/4}$ hours. Moving from unit $n=16$ to unit $n=256$ reduces the modeled completion time to exactly one quarter.
An online market has demand $q(p)=800p^{-1.2}$ for price $p>0$. Its constant price elasticity of demand is exactly $-1.2$.
A scientific response is $f(x)=x^{\pi}$ for $x>0$. A reviewer claims that it is not a power function because its exponent is irrational.
A calculator implements $f(x)=7x^{0}$ under standard real-arithmetic conventions. It must reject $x=0$, while returning $7$ for every nonzero input.
A sphere's volume is proportional to $r^{3}$. Increasing its radius by $2\%$ increases volume by exactly $6\%$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{H(256)}{H(16)}&=\left(\frac{256}{16}\right)^{-1/4} \\ &=16^{-1/4}=\frac12\ne\frac14
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d\ln q}{d\ln p}&=\frac{p}{q}\frac{dq}{dp}=-1.2
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=Ax^r \\ A&=1,\quad r=\pi\in\mathbb R
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{V(1.02r)}{V(r)}&=(1.02)^3=1.061208 \\ \text{increase}&=6.1208\%\ne6\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Learning curves, demand elasticity, irrational powers, and sensitivity.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 19
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A transport cost model is $C(x)=2x^{3}+5$. Because of the fixed charge, it cannot be represented by one pure power $Ax^{r}$ for all positive $x$.
A geometry program simplifies $f(x)=\sqrt{12x^{2}}$. It reports $f(x)=2\sqrt3\,x$ for every real input $x$, including negative inputs.
A calibration requires $5x^{-2}=45$ for a nonzero real setting $x$. The complete real solution set is $\{-1/3,1/3\}$.
An engineering model has strength proportional to $L^{2}$ and mass proportional to $L^{3}$. Increasing size by $20\%$ reduces strength per unit mass by exactly $20\%$.
A positive concentration map is $f(x)=x^{-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$. Applying the same map twice returns the original concentration, so the map is its own inverse.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{C(2x)}{C(x)}&=\frac{16x^3+5}{2x^3+5} \\ &\text{depends on }x,\ \text{unlike the constant }2^r
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{12x^2}&=2\sqrt3\,|x| \\ x<0&\Rightarrow |x|=-x\ne x
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
5x^{-2}&=45\Rightarrow x^{-2}=9 \\ x^2&=\frac19\Rightarrow x=\pm\frac13
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\text{new ratio}}{\text{old ratio}}&=(1.2)^{-1}=\frac56 \\ \text{decrease}&=1-\frac56=\frac16\approx16.67\%
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(f(x))&=f\left(\frac1x\right) \\ &=\left(\frac1x\right)^{-1}=x
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Identifying pure powers, radicals, negative powers, and self-inverse models.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 20
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A material response is $R(x)=7x^{4/5}$ for $x>0$. A scientist claims its graph is convex upward near $x=1$ because the exponent is positive.
A cubic resource model is proportional to $x^{3}$. Cutting the input by $60\%$ leaves less than one tenth of the original modeled resource.
A factory uses $Q(L)=20\sqrt L$ for $L\ge0$. A planner claims that every labour level $L\ge35$ guarantees output of at least $140$ units.
A researcher compares the readings $x^{2}$ and $x^{4}$ at the normalized input $x=0.6$. The fourth-power reading is strictly smaller than the square reading.
A reciprocal-square sensor uses $f(x)=3x^{-2}$ for $x>0$. At input $x=0.5$, a technician claims that the reading is exactly $6$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
R''(x)&=7\left(\frac45\right)\left(-\frac15\right)x^{-6/5} \\ R''(1)&=-\frac{28}{25}<0
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{R(0.4x)}{R(x)}&=(0.4)^3=0.064 \\ 0.064&<0.1
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
20\sqrt L&\ge140\Rightarrow\sqrt L\ge7 \\ L&\ge49,\ \text{not }L\ge35
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

$$
\begin{aligned}
(0.6)^2&=0.36 \\ (0.6)^4&=0.1296<0.36
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation verifies the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(0.5)&=3(0.5)^{-2}=3(4) \\ &=12\ne6
\end{aligned}
$$

The calculation contradicts the claim, so the statement is False.
